messages:
harper: tiny WFH triumph + humblebrag: mounted my router on a curtain rod using velcro strips and it fixed my dead corner. felt like MacGyver. :mechanical_arm: :curtain:

nina: velcro router perch? thats delightfully ridiculous. photo? :camera_with_flash:

harper: posted pic: http://imgur.com/placeholder_velcro (yes it looks very medical)

drew: nice. i zip-tied mine under the desk and now it overheats. pro tip: keep vents clear. also velcro means easy swap for firmware updates.

max: had to laugh because my cat Roxie thinks the velcro is a scratching toy. she pushed it off twice. solution: small safety tether + a gummy coin weight.

roxie: *meow of approval* (not really)
\nharper: safety tether is key. learned that the hard way when it tumbled into a pile of bills during a call. :sweat_smile:

ops-bot: ops-bot: Notifying users: ISP jitter detected 2027-01-11T16:05:00Z. Short packet spikes 16:04:5816:06:30 UTC affecting residential cluster W5. Monitoring.

nina: that matches my timeline. had two reconnects at 16:05. good to know it wasn't my velcro engineering.

drew: also FYI if you're moving your router, re-run `sudo iw reg set US` if you're in the US and seeing weird channel drops after location change. saved me once.

harper: adding small checklist to #devex: "Velcro perch safety: 1) keep vents clear, 2) secure with tether, 3) test for heat, 4) label cords." happy to share photos and measurements if anyone wants to replicate.

max: kudos to harper for the creative fix and for returning my borrowed dongle last week. :heart:

roxie: also demands more treats for engineering support. :cat2:

harper: thanks team! will retire the temporary pizza-box reflector and keep velcro as plan B. :tada:
